title: A created version is not the live deployment target
environment: Apps Script deployment plus Dify integration. Do not confuse draft execution with a published API surface or infer authentication failure before the intended version is reachable.
goal: Observe new build/authentication diagnostics through an existing integration endpoint.
approach: Historical failed assumption: Version creation or propagation delay was treated as equivalent to updating the endpoint's deployment target.
what_worked: Historical correction: Require the exact existing deployment to reference the intended version, then preserve required diagnostics end to end. This was the recorded recovery plan, not a completed live repair at that checkpoint. Verification reported by the source: Read-only version/deployment and endpoint-identity comparisons established the mismatch. Seventeen local tests passed but did not assert the full new response; no corrected live result was established there.
what_failed: Historical observed failure: Expected diagnostics were absent even though the new immutable service version existed.
why: Confirmed: deployment metadata still pointed to the previous version. Separately, workflow parser/final-output definitions dropped the new diagnostic fields. The exact failed operator step was unknown.
improved_method: Verify control-plane target and observed runtime marker separately. Waiting cannot fix metadata that still selects the old version.
when_to_use: Apps Script deployment plus Dify integration. Do not confuse draft execution with a published API surface or infer authentication failure before the intended version is reachable.
when_not_to_use: Do not confuse draft execution with a published API surface or infer authentication failure before the intended version is reachable.
known_limitations: This is an independently curated generalization of an earlier recorded failure. No source-side experiment was rerun during this registration; observation_date is the 2026-10-09 knowledge-review date, not the incident date. Applicability and root-cause claims remain limited to the source-reported conditions.
